old: Treat a lesion that is persistently larger than 5 cm, or growing by 20% or more, as an indication for curative treatment — and say plainly, to the patient and in the note, that 5 cm is a convention and not a derived threshold.
concise: Persistent size >5 cm or growth ≥20% is an indication for curative treatment. Explain that 5 cm is a conventional threshold.
new: Assess resection for a persistently ≥5 cm or growing adenoma after appropriate risk-factor modification; account for subtype, sex, symptoms, bleeding and suspicion of malignancy.

old: Reimage with contrast-enhanced MRI at 6 months, and treat that scan as a trajectory rather than a verdict — six months is too early to call risk-factor modification a failure.
concise: Repeat contrast MRI at 6 months; assess trajectory. This is too early to declare risk-factor modification unsuccessful.
new: Reimage after risk-factor modification and assess the trajectory. In women with lesions ≥5 cm, individualize reassessment and intervention over 6–12 months unless bleeding, concerning growth or suspected malignancy requires earlier action.

old: State the actual evidence for the threshold when you offer observation: three uncontrolled cohorts with two to four years of follow-up, no randomised comparison, and not one direct comparison of the two strategies in any of them.
concise: Observation evidence: three uncontrolled cohorts, 2–4 years follow-up; no randomized or direct strategy comparison.
new: Explain that observation evidence is nonrandomized: prospective cohorts have short follow-up, and Sadot provides a retrospective size-matched observation-versus-resection comparison.

old: In MEN1, resect a functional tumour whatever its size, observe a nonfunctional tumour under 1 cm, and resect above 2 cm or on significant growth — accepting that surgery will not clear the gland.
concise: MEN1: resect functional tumors at any size; observe nonfunctional <1 cm; resect >2 cm or significant growth. Surgery will not clear the gland.
new: In MEN1, individualize treatment by functional syndrome and hereditary context. Symptomatic insulinoma generally requires treatment; MEN1 gastrinoma timing and extent remain controversial. Nonfunctioning lesions may be observed when small, with resection considered for size, growth and other concerning features. Surgery will not clear the inherited risk.

old: Resect, in a patient fit for pancreatectomy, for jaundice with a head cyst, an enhancing mural nodule of 5 mm or more or a solid component, a main pancreatic duct of 10 mm or more, or cytology suspicious or positive for high-grade dysplasia or carcinoma.
concise: If fit for pancreatectomy, resect for: jaundice with a head cyst; enhancing mural nodule ≥5 mm or solid component; main duct ≥10 mm; or suspicious/positive high-grade dysplasia/carcinoma cytology.
new: Obtain surgical assessment for a high-risk stigma: obstructive jaundice with a head cyst, an enhancing mural nodule ≥5 mm or solid component, main pancreatic duct ≥10 mm, or cytology suspicious or positive for high-grade dysplasia or carcinoma. Consider resection when clinically appropriate after assessing fitness, comorbidity, life expectancy and preference.
